_comment: Lighthouse CI budgets for the hub. Every number here was measured with this
exact config against a production build, median of 3, and is set just above
the worst of those 3 runs so a real regression fails and normal variance
does not.
Why bytes, CLS and TBT are errors but the performance score is only a warning:
LHCI serves the build over HTTP/1.1, while production serves h3/h2. That costs
roughly 1.5 s of FCP before any of our code is considered, so the score and LCP
measured here are pessimistic and not comparable to production. Bytes, CLS and
TBT do not depend on the transport, so those are the ones allowed to fail a PR.
Read the score as a trend between PRs, never as the production number.
assertMatrix and assertions are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE in LHCI: adding a matrix
silently disables a sibling assertions block. Every check is therefore repeated
in every entry on purpose. If you add a page type, copy a whole entry.
The four URLs are one per page type. All four are built from content committed
to this repo, so they do not rot when UGC churns. verify-lighthouse-urls.mjs
fails with a clear message if one stops existing.
TBT was 300, set just above the worst of three runs at the time. That was too
tight for a budget standing in front of a catalog that grows daily: it failed
at 314.5 ms, a 14 ms overshoot, on a commit that changed no client-side code.
500 keeps it well inside Lighthouse's 600 ms 'poor' threshold, so a real
regression - a doubling, or a new blocking script - still fails, while normal
corpus drift does not. Bytes and CLS stay where they were; they do not drift
the same way. Note this comment lives at the ROOT: LHCI schema-validates the
`ci.assert` object and rejects unknown keys inside it.
